skill: Evaluate dy/dx=f(x,y) at three isolated points and identify the diagram with those segment slopes.
reasoning_steps: Read each indicated coordinate from the diagram or prompt.
Substitute both coordinates into f, preserving signs, powers and denominators.
Translate positive, negative and zero values and magnitudes to local segment directions.
Choose the unique matching image among five and explain all three substitutions.
response_contract: Observed exercise bank: one radio selection among five image choices. Canonical example requests a sketch and supplies a worked diagram; it has no answer field.
difficulty: Easy: three small-coordinate substitutions; polynomial, bilinear and simple rational expressions; no integration, qualitative regional analysis, or full-grid plotting.
invariants: Three finite defined slopes at distinct isolated points.
One mathematically correct image out of five for exercise questions.
The equation, coordinates, drawn segment slopes, key and substitution solution agree.
Retain both-coordinate dependence and the observed arithmetic workload.
essential_constraints: Slope is f(x,y), not y/x or a solution curve.
For a denominator x, selected x cannot be zero.
Coordinate plotting uses equal axis scale so segment angle represents the stated slope.
incidental_assignments: Which point has a zero, positive or negative slope is not fixed by the skill.
The correct diagram's position and which points distractors corrupt are incidental.
The source coordinates, coefficient signs, individual zero counts and exact equation coefficients are example assignments, eligible to change while preserving workload.
permitted_variations: Small signed integer coordinates and modest integer/fraction coefficients in the observed linear, bilinear, x-squared-minus-y, difference-of-squares, and y-squared-over-x families.
Change target point sets, slope signs, zero counts and locations; derive diagram, solution and answer together.
Shuffle complete image banks and change plausible wrong slopes without changing the response contract.
